correctness.rationale: Each open-neighborhood tetrahedron is {v_{a±1,i}, v_{a,i±1}}. A pair of distinct same-column other-row vertices has unique common neighbor at the given column, proving all 3n triangle-tetrahedron and 3n edge-triangle pairs are legitimate elementary collapses. Residual triangles triangulate two parity sheets of the planar diamond tiling; even deck lattice of <(3,0),(0,n)> has minimum nonzero Manhattan length >=6 for n=3 or >=5, guaranteeing no erroneous quotient identifications. Odd period (3,0) swaps sheets, giving a connected orientation-preserving quotient torus and f=(3n,9n,6n). n=4 has (12,42,48,12) and chi6. The graph is 4-regular, but for n>=6 and 3|n, triangle columns are characteristic and Aut(G)=S3×D_n has no order3n element, hence not circulant. Independently checked actual neighborhood face vectors and core incidence for n=3,4,5,6,7,9,12,25. Infinite conclusion uses lattice proof, not finite sampling.
